title: Reading Input (scanf)
instructions: So far the program does all the talking. scanf lets the USER talk back by typing something.
scanf("%d", &age) reads a number the user types and stores it in age.
Notice the & — scanf needs the ADDRESS of the box so it knows where to put what it reads. This is why you learned pointers first!
Note: this practice window can't easily take typed input while it runs, so just get it to compile and run here. To truly try it, run the program in a terminal and type a number.
The pattern is the important part to remember.
task: Fill in the scanf so it reads a number into age. (It just needs to compile and run here.)
hint:
Pass the format and the ADDRESS of age:

    scanf("%d", &age);
